rangesFor: Dynamic DSC at about 10 K/min. Temperatures are the peak temperature of an event, in degrees C.

events.name: Melting
events.notes: Melting of a crystalline phase absorbs heat and gives an endotherm without any mass loss, so it is invisible to TGA. A single crystalline material gives a sharp, narrow peak; polymers, fats and waxes give broad, sometimes shallow, peaks from their varied crystalline structure.
events.source: Direction: Gaisford, Kett & Haines (2016) §5.5.1 (melting, sharp for a single crystalline material, broad for polymers, fats and waxes) and §3.5 (no mass change with melting). Temperature range: TODO, verify (the book gives no general range).

events.name: Dehydration or evaporation (loss of water or solvent)
events.notes: Loss of water or solvent absorbs heat and is accompanied by a mass loss in TGA. In a vented pan moisture gives a small broad endotherm; a lid with a pinhole sharpens the peaks and can shift them to higher temperatures. It can be confused with melting: TGA tells them apart (a mass loss). Example from the source: CuSO4·5H2O loses its water in three main steps up to 300 °C at 5 °C/min.
events.source: Direction: Gaisford, Kett & Haines (2016) §5.5.5 (loss of volatiles is endothermic; CuSO4·5H2O example) and §5.5.6 (moisture gives a small broad endotherm at about 50 to 80 °C in a vented pan). Temperature range: TODO, verify (the book gives no general range).

events.name: Crystallisation (cold crystallisation on heating, or from the melt on cooling)
events.notes: Crystallisation releases heat and gives an exotherm without any mass loss. On heating it is called cold crystallisation and follows the glass transition; on cooling it appears when the melt crystallises.
events.source: Direction and scans: Gaisford, Kett & Haines (2016) §5.5.3 (crystallisation is exothermic, on cooling or as cold crystallisation on heating). Temperature range: TODO, verify (the book gives no general range).

events.name: Oxidation or combustion
events.notes: Needs oxygen: an exotherm with a mass loss (burning of organic material) or a mass gain (oxidation of a metal or lower oxide) in TGA. Not expected in nitrogen or argon.
events.source: Direction: Gaisford, Kett & Haines (2016) §11.2.6 (oxidation of carbons is an exothermic gas-solid reaction) and §5.7.1 (oxidative induction time). Temperature range: TODO, verify (the book gives no general range).

events.name: Solid-solid phase transition
events.notes: A change of crystal structure without melting and without mass change. It can be endothermic or exothermic and often shows a thermal lag between heating and cooling.
events.source: TODO, verify: neither the direction nor the range is checked against a source.

events.name: Decomposition
events.notes: Usually accompanied by a mass loss in TGA. Often endothermic in an inert gas; in air the products can burn, which adds an exotherm.
events.source: Direction 'either': Gaisford, Kett & Haines (2016) §3.5, Figure 3.19 (TG-DSC of a flame retardant: an endothermic change with mass loss, then an exothermic decomposition). Temperature range: TODO, verify (the book gives no general range).
